mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the graphical addition of vectors using the tip‑to‑tail method with the parallelogram method?

options.A: Both methods give the same magnitude and direction for the resultant vector.
options.B: The tip‑to‑tail method gives only the magnitude, while the parallelogram method gives only the direction.
options.C: The tip‑to‑tail method works only for two vectors, whereas the parallelogram method works for any number of vectors.
options.D: The tip‑to‑tail method is an algebraic technique, while the parallelogram method is purely graphical.

mcqs.answer: Both methods give the same magnitude and direction for the resultant vector.
mcqs.explanation: Both the tip‑to‑tail (head‑to‑tail) method and the parallelogram method are graphical ways of adding vectors. When the vectors are placed correctly, each method yields a resultant that has exactly the same magnitude and direction; they are simply two different constructions of the same resultant. Options B, C and D describe incorrect distinctions.

mcqs.question: If \(\vec A = 5\hat i + 2\hat j\) and \(\vec B = 3\hat i - 4\hat j\), what is the vector that represents \(\vec A - \vec B\)?
mcqs.explanation: Vector subtraction is performed component‑wise: \(\vec A - \vec B = (5-3)\hat i + (2-(-4))\hat j = 2\hat i + 6\hat j\). Option A matches this result. The other options arise from incorrect sign handling or swapping components.

mcqs.question: According to the triangle law of vector addition, the resultant of two vectors is represented by which of the following?

options.A: The diagonal of the parallelogram formed by the two vectors.
options.B: The third side of a triangle when the two vectors are placed head to tail.
options.C: The sum of the magnitudes of the two vectors.
options.D: The vector opposite to the sum of the two vectors.

mcqs.answer: The third side of a triangle when the two vectors are placed head to tail.
mcqs.explanation: The triangle law states that if two vectors are placed consecutively (head to tail), the vector that closes the triangle (the third side) represents their resultant. Option A describes the parallelogram law, while C and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: The parallelogram law of vector addition states that when two vectors are represented as adjacent sides of a parallelogram, the resultant vector is:

options.A: The diagonal drawn from the common origin of the two vectors.
options.B: The diagonal drawn from the opposite corner of the parallelogram.
options.C: The sum of the magnitudes of the two vectors.
options.D: The vector opposite to the sum of the two vectors.

mcqs.answer: The diagonal drawn from the opposite corner of the parallelogram.
mcqs.explanation: In the parallelogram method, the two vectors are placed tail to tail. The resultant is the diagonal that starts from the common tail and ends at the opposite corner of the parallelogram. Option A describes the starting point, not the resultant. Options C and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the polygon law of vector addition from the triangle law?

options.A: The polygon law applies only to three vectors, whereas the triangle law applies to any number of vectors.
options.B: The polygon law involves arranging vectors head to tail to form a closed polygon, while the triangle law uses only two vectors.
options.C: The polygon law gives only the magnitude of the resultant, whereas the triangle law gives both magnitude and direction.
options.D: The polygon law is used for scalar addition, while the triangle law is used for vector addition.

mcqs.answer: The polygon law involves arranging vectors head to tail to form a closed polygon, while the triangle law uses only two vectors.
mcqs.explanation: The polygon law generalises the triangle law: any number of vectors can be placed head‑to‑tail to form a closed polygon; the vector that closes the polygon is the resultant. The triangle law is a special case with just two vectors. Options A, C, and D misstate the definitions.

mcqs.question: Two vectors \(\vec P = 3\hat i + 4\hat j\) and \(\vec Q = -2\hat i + 1\hat j\) act on a particle. What is the magnitude and direction (measured from the positive x‑axis) of the resultant \(\vec R = \vec P + \vec Q\)?

options.A: Magnitude \(\sqrt{26}\) and direction \(\approx 78.7^{\circ}\) above the x‑axis.
options.B: Magnitude 5 and direction 45° above the x‑axis.
options.C: Magnitude \(\sqrt{13}\) and direction \(\approx 63.4^{\circ}\) above the x‑axis.
options.D: Magnitude \(\sqrt{26}\) and direction \(\approx 11.3^{\circ}\) above the x‑axis.

mcqs.answer: Magnitude \(\sqrt{26}\) and direction \(\approx 78.7^{\circ}\) above the x‑axis.
mcqs.explanation: Resultant components: \(R_x = 3 + (-2) = 1\), \(R_y = 4 + 1 = 5\). Magnitude \(|\vec R| = \sqrt{1^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{26}\). Direction \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(5/1) \approx 78.7^{\circ}\). Option A matches these calculations. The other options contain incorrect magnitudes or angles.

mcqs.question: Two forces of 10 N act on a particle: one directed due east and the other due north. Using graphical addition, what is the magnitude of the resultant force?
mcqs.explanation: When two equal forces act at right angles, the resultant is the diagonal of a square with side 10 N. Magnitude = \(\sqrt{10^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{200} \approx 14.14\) N. Option B is correct. Option A is just one component, C would be the sum if they were collinear, and D would be the case for opposite equal forces.

mcqs.question: A hiker walks 7 km east and then 3 km north. Another hiker walks 2 km east and 5 km north from the same starting point. What is the displacement vector of the first hiker relative to the second hiker?
mcqs.explanation: Relative displacement = \(\vec R_1 - \vec R_2\). \(\vec R_1 = 7\hat i + 3\hat j\), \(\vec R_2 = 2\hat i + 5\hat j\). Subtracting gives \((7-2)\hat i + (3-5)\hat j = 5\hat i - 2\hat j\). Hence option A is correct. The other options arise from incorrect subtraction or sign errors.
